title: HF Sinclair — Second Insider Cluster on Q2 EPS Blowout
summary: DINO Q2 2026 delivered adj EPS $5.31 vs $4.60 est (+15%), EBITDA doubled to $1.5B, and management raised the dividend 5%. A fresh 2-insider cluster on 2026-08-11 (~$2.4M at $76.68) confirms management's inside view that crack spreads and mid-continent refining margins hold into H2. Promoted from Stalking (2026-06-27) on the second-cluster + Q2-blowout promotion trigger.
catalyst: Two catalysts converged: (1) Q2 2026 print on 2026-07-29 — adj net income +198% YoY to $960M ($5.31 EPS vs $4.60 est), EBITDA $1.5B, 5% dividend hike to $0.525, $265M returned to shareholders. (2) 2-insider cluster purchase of ~$2.4M on 2026-08-11 at avg $76.68 — first material cluster since the original June 2026 buys that seeded the Stalking entry. Q3 crack spread datapoints (weekly EIA) and Q3 earnings in late-October are the next dated tests.
thesis: Refining is mid-to-late cycle globally, but US mid-continent refiners with logistical advantage (DINO's Salt Lake / Tulsa / Casper system) are structurally advantaged when WTI-Brent widens post-Hormuz and when export-parity Gulf products stay firm. Q2 confirmed cash generation is robust — insider buying AFTER the beat and dividend raise signals management believes crack spreads persist beyond consensus's H2 fade thesis. Renewable diesel is now a real earnings contributor rather than a burden. Distinct from our upstream (LNG, ethane, shale) energy opps — this is downstream refining with different demand elasticity.
counter_thesis: Crack spreads mean-revert. The Q2 blowout was driven by 'steady demand, tight supply, favorable crack spreads' — every one of those is cyclical and reverses. Stock has already run to $87.93, within 7% of the 52-week high $94.22, and the market 'shrugged off' the profit surge (Simply Wall St headline) which signals institutions are already fading the peak. Refiners historically top out on beat-and-fade Q2/Q3 prints. Renewable diesel margins remain vulnerable to LCFS credit price and BTC/PTC policy changes. If Q3 EPS reverts to $3.50 the stock re-rates to $70.

ticker_rationale.DINO: Mid-continent refiner with the tightest cost advantage when WTI-Brent widens; renewable diesel now a durable cash contributor; Q2 EPS $5.31 crushed $4.60 est; screener WATCH (52 score) but the trade is cyclical not compounder. Forward P/E 9x with $265M/quarter buyback+dividend.

trade_construction.target_12mo: DINO $110 (+25%) — 10x forward EPS on FY27E ~$11, assumes crack spreads hold above $18/bbl through H1 2027 and buyback pace sustained
trade_construction.stop_loss: DINO $73 (-17%) — closes below the pre-Q2-print consolidation and 200-day MA; signals crack spreads have cratered faster than expected and Q3 will disappoint
trade_construction.position_size_pct: 0.5-1.0% (On Our Radar; cyclical position warrants smaller sizing than compounder plays)

confidence_note: This is a cyclical Q2-blowout chase entry — market skepticism about crack-spread durability is the key risk. Would firm up to High Conviction if: (a) Q3 EIA weekly crack spread data (mid-cycle ~$18-22/bbl reference) holds through September, or (b) DINO pulls back to the $76-80 zone (insider cost basis) without a bearish Q3 pre-announce. Ledger note: refining pattern (Cyclical) has n=1 in ledger — no historical hit rate to calibrate against yet, so treat as new pattern.
